description: Standalone, proposals-only Living Context check: bind a workspace/repository to an exact Git revision and bounded changed surfaces; read selected Knowledge roots only at that revision; recall contextual claims with authority and retrieval provenance; reconcile only affected claims; and emit minimal owning-source update proposals. This is contextual recall/currentness, not a Surface trust derivation. It reuses Ops #121 holds/broken/unverifiable only as consumer vocabulary and does not create a trust authority.

expects.description: The input binds workspace, repository, exact Git commit SHA, changed surfaces or diff, target audience, and selected Knowledge roots/providers. The adapter verifies the named worktree and raw commit object, clears inherited Git overrides, disables replace/graft semantics, then reads only git-show <sha>:<path>; it never falls through to the working tree.

Each recalled claim carries current, superseded, or unverifiable contextual status, its authoritative citation, and retrieval provenance. A superseded claim is never returned as current; every missing requested claim id is its own explicit no-answer/unverifiable entry and makes the result not_verified.

Only claims whose declared affected surfaces intersect the bounded change are reconciled, preserving every intersection. An intersection is neutral affected/requires-reconciliation, never an inferred contradicted or broken verdict; contradicted requires explicit authoritative fixture evidence. Affected unverifiable claims route to their owner without trust derivation. Holds, broken, and unverifiable are documented consumer vocabulary from Ops #121, not a new trust derivation.

The adapter emits only minimal proposed updates routed to each claim's owning source and writes only new no-follow files under an explicit private run/proposal directory after rejecting symlink components or targets. It never edits documentation, decisions, or Knowledge records.
